MISCELLANEOUS

EXPLOSIVES AND GUN POWDER ON A GERMAN STEAMER.

The Sin Wan Pao, the China Times and other local
newspapers publish the following report:-
Acting on secret information to the effect that a
large quantity of firearms, ordered by a certain party
from Germany, is being transported on board the s.s.
Recanver and that the vessel is about to arrive at Woosung,
the Ministry of Navy has sent the gunboat "Hai Yung" to wait
outside Woosung.
At midnight October 22/3 the German vessel was noticed
proceeding in the direction of Shanghai. She was detained
and a search revealed a large quantity of explosives
and gun powder consigned to Korea, Dairen and other
places. The contraband was later moved removed. An
investigation is being made.

Made by Temp. Cl. Ass't Cook. Forwarded by Tho Robertson C.D.I.

The Norwegian ship "Frey," 4700 tons dead weight
carrying a cargo of arms and ammunition, which put in at
Singapore on September 10 with engine trouble, is now reported
to have touched at Haifong where she discharged half of her
cargo, after which she proceeded to Newchwang where she
unloaded a part of the arms and ammunition. She then left
for Chinwangtao where she delivered the balance.

This action is explained as being the result of the
difficulty of receiving the money balance- 50% cash on
delivery- by the shippers from the Chinese end and is also
attributed to these latter now "confiscating" such cargoes.

The arms and ammunition stored at Haifong are under
French protection and the shippers will have to pay only
the storage due.

The above arms deal was arranged by the Frenchman
Monsieur Verondort, the former French Consul at Shanghai,
who was responsible for the famous s.s. "Praga" arms
consignment to China in January 1928.

Seizure At Chinwangtao
Of German Shipment Stirs
Criticisms Of Newspaper

Authorities Confiscate Goods Consigned To
Mukden Arsenal Which Were Withheld
When Payment Was Not Made.

(Reuter's Pacific Service)
Tientsin, September 13.—The Peking & Tientsin Times to-day sharply criticises the action taken in connection with some German goods which recently arrived at Chinwangtao.
A German firm, says the newspaper, recently imported, under a regular "Huchao," some "goods" for the Mukden Arsenal. Pending the liquidation of outstanding indebtedness, the firm stored the goods in the godowns of the Kailan Mining Administration. Last Wednesday a party of Manchu soldiers, accompanied by officials who alleged that they were acting under orders from Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang entered the godown and, in spite of the protests made by the agents, removed the 201 cases stored there by the German firm to the nearest military Yamen.
The Native Customs has since produced a lengthy communication alleging that the cargo has been confiscated as contraband, so as to prevent it falling into the hands of bad characters.

reasons are as follows:-

(a) No effort was made by those who were in possession
of the arms to bring them ashore. The ship arriv-
ed at 6 a.m. and was due to sail about 6 hours
later. The Police and Preventive Officers did not
begin their search until about 11-30 a.m., and
thus for 5½ hours no attempt had been made to
smuggle the goods ashore. The search made was very
hurriedly carried out, the departure of the ship
being delayed about a couple of hours.

(b) No very elaborate precautions have been taken to
conceal the arms. They were found in the locked
boxes of certain members of the crew. The crew
could hardly have suspected that a search would be
made, and did not therefore take the trouble to
conceal the arms more effectively.

(c) Had there been a conspiracy to import arms into
this country, the smugglers, in my opinion, would
not have brought them in a ship that was to remain
only a few hours at the Ballard Pier, immediately
opposite the Custom house. The landing of the arms
would have had to be carried out under the most
difficult circumstances. A ship would rather
have been selected that was to remain in dock for
some days.

(d) The smugglers themselves would have little opportuni-
-ty of landing their cargo in large quantities in
view of the fact that they would be on duty in con-
nection with the hurried arrival and departure of
the ship.

The information on which action was taken was not
received first hand, but there was good reason for supposing
that all the arms originally brought from Europe had not
been seized. It was estimated - though no definite informa-
tion is available on the point - that there were originally

理由如下：

(a) 持有军火的人并未试图将其带上岸。该船于
上午6点抵达，预计约6小时后
启航。警察和预防性官员直到
上午11:30左右才开始搜查，因此
在5½小时内无人尝试将货物走私上岸。搜查进行得
非常匆忙，导致船只离港延误
约两小时。

(b)  conceal 军火的预防措施并不十分周密。它们是在
某些船员的上锁箱子中发现的。船员
几乎不可能预料到会受到搜查，因此
并未费心更有效地隐藏军火。

(c) 如果存在向本国进口军火的阴谋，依我看，
走私者不会选择一艘仅在巴拉德码头（Ballard Pier）
停留几小时的船只，该码头正对着
海关大楼。在这样的情况下卸载军火
将面临极大的困难。他们本应选择
一艘将在码头停留数日的船只。

(d) 鉴于走私者本人忙于应对
船只匆忙抵离的相关勤务，他们几乎没有机会
大量卸载货物。

采取行动的资讯并非直接获得，但有充分理由推测，
最初从欧洲带来的所有军火并未全部被查获。据估计——尽管
对此点并无确切信息——最初约有

It is not unreasonable to suppose that should any
member of the crew now in illegal possession of a weapon find

A GERMAN “PIRATE”
SHIP

Venezuelan Raider at Port of
Spain: Falke Supposed to
Have Arms for China

Mystery surrounds the status of
the German steamship Falke,
which has been branded as a
“pirate,” by the Venezuelan
Government, with the consequent
penalties for the crew, on account
of the insurgent raid recently
carried out at Cumana. The Falke
is now anchored in Port of Spain,
Trinidad, and officials there are
puzzled as to how she should be
treated. The crew is divided, the
officers denouncing Captain Tipplitz,
who, they contend, led them into
trouble without their knowledge.
They have consulted the German
Consul at Port of Spain to deter-
mine what action to take against
the captain.

According to the officers’ story
they left Hamburg in ballast for
Gdynia, Poland, where they took
aboard 125 Venezuelan exiles,
headed by General Delgado Chal-
baud and his son. Thence they
proceeded to Cumana, Venezuela,
near which place they took aboard
200 other insurgents and a large
quantity of ammunition. They con-
tend they were forced to land this
with the rebels in the abortive
attempt to seize Cumana, in the
process of which the vessel’s third
officer was killed at the helm.
Government troops routed the
insurgents. Chalbaud’s son, with a
small group, succeeded in regaining
the Falke, which took them to
Grenada.

The Venezuelan Government has
asked all Governments to proceed
against her. The fact that the
Falke was apparently obtained for
the express purpose of raiding
Cumana puts a different complexion
on the first reports, which told of
the seizure of the vessel by
insurgents near Cumana, and its
subsequent use in the raid.

A Rumour Recalled

To whom does the rebel ship
Falke belong? The German authori-
ties are still in the dark as to which
German company owns her and as
to the details of her adventurous
voyage, states a Berlin message.
The German Government is par-
ticularly desirous of bringing to
book any Germans who had a hand
in the buccaneering adventure.
Official sources state that the
Venezuelan Government has not
protested to the German Govern-
ment, as stated in some reports.

Before the Falke left Gdynia, in
Poland, the German Communist
Press wrote sensational stories of
how the ship (which it declared
belonged to the North German
Lloyd) contained “an enormous
shipment of guns and machine-gun
munitions” destined to arm China.

一艘德国“海盗”船

委内瑞拉袭击者现身西班牙港：据信“法尔克”号载有运往中国的武器

德国蒸汽船“法尔克”号（Falke）的地位笼罩在谜团之中。该船被委内瑞拉政府贴上“海盗”标签，船员因此面临相应惩罚，原因是最近在该国库马纳（Cumana）发动的叛乱袭击。目前，“法尔克”号停泊在特立尼达的西班牙港（Port of Spain），当地官员对如何处置该船感到困惑。船员内部发生分裂，高级船员谴责蒂普利茨（Tipplitz）船长，称他在船员不知情的情况下将他们带入困境。他们已咨询德国驻西班牙港领事，以确定对船长采取何种行动。

据高级船员讲述，他们离开汉堡时未装载货物，前往波兰格丁尼亚（Gdynia），在那里搭载了125名委内瑞拉流亡者，由德尔加多·查尔鲍德（Delgado Chalbaud）将军及其儿子率领。随后，他们驶往委内瑞拉库马纳，并在附近搭载了另外200名叛乱分子和大量弹药。他们声称，在试图夺取库马纳的失败尝试中，他们被迫与叛乱分子一起将这些物资卸上岸，在此过程中，该船的三副在舵位上丧生。政府军击溃了叛乱分子。查尔鲍德的儿子带领一小群人成功夺回“法尔克”号，该船将他们带往格林纳达。

委内瑞拉政府已要求各国政府对该船采取行动。“法尔克”号显然是为了袭击库马纳这一特定目的而获得的，这一事实使最初的报道呈现出不同的面貌，最初报道称该船是在库马纳附近被叛乱分子劫持，随后用于袭击。

 recalled 的一则谣言

叛乱船只“法尔克”号归谁所有？据柏林消息，德国当局仍不清楚哪家德国公司拥有该船，也不清楚其冒险航行的细节。德国政府特别希望将任何参与此次海盗冒险的德国人绳之以法。官方消息来源称，正如某些报道所述，委内瑞拉政府并未向德国政府提出抗议。

在“法尔克”号离开波兰格丁尼亚之前，德国共产党媒体曾撰写耸人听闻的故事，称该船（宣称属于北德意志劳埃德公司 North German Lloyd）装有“大批枪支和机枪弹药”，旨在武装中国。

ARMS FOR CHINA

ALLEGED GERMAN SHIPMENT

The Act placing German nationals in Germany and abroad under the obligation to refrain from taking any part in the delivery of arms to China has lapsed. The Act, by the passage of which Germany adhered to the Peking Agreement of 1919 between Great Britain, the United States and five other Powers, contained a clause stating that it would remain in force until May 1, 1929, and could be prolonged by decree. As it has not been prolonged it has automatically lapsed.

The Danzig correspondent of the Communist paper "Rote Fahne," alleges that the North German Lloyd steamer, Falke, left the Polish harbour of Gdynia for China with a large consignment of ammunition. The paper recalls that under an agreement reached two years ago with the shipping companies, the latter undertook not to transport arms or ammunition to China from German harbours. The "Rote Fahne" now asserts that the Falke's captain, recognising the impossibility of obtaining a German crew, tried his luck in Danzig, but the sailors there also refused, "out of solidarity with the Soviets." The captain was finally compelled to go to Gdynia, and hire a crew of Poles.

The North German Lloyd categorically denies the above report. It says the Falke, which has a cargo capacity of only 997 tons, is proceeding to London and not to China.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, AUGUST 22, 1929

ARMS HAUL MADE AT
HONGKONG

111 Pistols, 11,000 Rounds
Of Ammunition
Seized

Hongkong, Aug. 16.
As the result of information
received, Revenue Officers were
engaged the whole of yesterday
searching for arms on board the
Douglas' s.s. Haiching, which
makes regular runs between Hong-
kong, Swatow, Amoy and Foochow.
After a long and thorough
search in which practically every
inch of the vessel was gone over
the Revenue men were rewarded
for their patience by the discovery
of the contraband in one of the
coal bunkers.
Four sacks were hauled on deck,
and when these were opened there
were brought to light 111 automa-
tic pistols of French make and
11,000 rounds of ammunition.
Inquiries were then made on
board but the arms could not be
traced to any individual. The
Revenue men took their "find"
ashore and stored the pistols and
ammunition in the Import and
Export Office.

Two Firemen Missing
Later the Police took up the
investigation with a view to dis-
covering those responsible for the
placing of the contraband on board,
and then it was discovered, after
a muster was taken, that two of
the ship's firemen had absconded.
The Haiching leaves for the
Chinese ports above-mentioned to-
day, and the inference is that the
arms and ammunition which had
doubtlessly been smuggled into
Hongkong on some large ocean
going vessel, had been transferred
to the Haiching unknown to her
Officers, for eventual smuggling
into one of the Chinese ports.
This morning the arms and
ammunition were transferred to
Police Headquarters in the I. & E.
Department's "Grey Maria."

Application To Court
Then Revenue Officer Grimmit
made an application before Mr. E.
W. Hamilton, at the Central
Magistracy, for an order for the
confiscation of the contraband.
After taking evidence that the
arms and ammunition were found
on the Haiching and that they
were not claimed. Mr. Hamilton
made the necessary confiscation
order, after which the contraband
was transferred to the Police
armoury.

香港查获武器

缴获111支手枪，11,000发子弹

香港，8月16日。
根据收到的情报，税务人员昨天全天在道格拉斯轮船公司（Douglas' s.s.）的“海清”号（Haiching）轮船上搜寻武器，该船定期往返于香港、汕头、厦门和福州之间。
经过长时间彻底的搜查，几乎检查了船上的每一寸地方，税务人员的耐心得到了回报，他们在其中一个煤舱中发现了违禁品。
四袋物品被拖到甲板上，打开后，露出了111支法国制造的自动手枪和11,000发子弹。
随后在船上进行了查询，但无法将武器追溯到任何个人。税务人员将他们的“发现”带上岸，并将手枪和弹药存放在进出口办事处。

两名司炉失踪
随后，警方介入调查，以期找出负责将违禁品装上船的人，经点名后发现，船上的两名司炉已潜逃。
“海清”号今天驶往上述中国港口，由此推断，这些武器和弹药无疑是通过某艘大型远洋轮船走私进入香港的，然后在船员不知情的情况下转移到“海清”号上，以便最终走私进入其中一个中国港口。
今天上午，武器和弹药通过进出口处的“格雷玛丽亚”号（Grey Maria）转移至警察总局。

向法院申请
随后，税务官员格里米特（Grimmit）向中央裁判司署的 E. W. Hamilton 先生提出申请，请求下令没收违禁品。
在取证确认武器和弹药是在“海清”号上发现且无人认领后，Hamilton 先生作出了必要的没收令，随后违禁品被转移至警察军械库。

TRANSLATION OF EXTRACTS FROM FRENCH POLICE INTELLIGENCE REPORT.

August 6, 1929.

At the conference over the disbandment and reorganization of the National forces, Chiang Kai Shek and other members of the National Government resolved that 7/10ths of the troops be disbanded and to retain 800,000 men as Government troops.

Yen Sih San has telegraphed to the Government stating that the soldiers of Feng Yu Hsiang will not observe the Government's orders as regards disbandment and reorganization.

The National Government has instructed the Peking-Hankow Railway not to remit to Feng Yu Hsiang the monthly contribution of $300,000 for military expenses. The remittance to Yen Sih San, however, will not be stopped.

The troops of the Third Group under Yen Sih San will be disbanded and reorganized within two months. As soon as this has been done, Yen Sih San will go abroad with Feng Yu Hsiang.

Soong Ts Van, Minister of Finance, in agreement with the various banks of Shanghai, will issue $5,000,000 worth of bonds in Shanghai to cover the expenses for the disbandment and reorganization of troops. 50% of the bonds will be placed on the market during this month.

At 2 p.m. yesterday a meeting was held by representatives of 17 labour unions, namely, the Commercial Press Workers Union, the Linotype Workers Union, the Union of Workers of the Chapei Electricity and Waterworks Co. etc. at the office of the Union of Workers of Foreign and Chinese Piece Goods Shops at No. 13 Po Zeng Tse Li, Kwaching Road, Chapei. Zing Pah Yai, of the Piece Goods Union, presided.

One of the resolutions passed was as follows:-
"That the Social Bureau and the Shanghai Special District Kuomintang be informed, in the name of the various labour unions in Chapei, that the Sixth District Kuomintang is oppressing the various labour unions."

（批：D.1.2 / Police culs / to Majumi / +2）

380 cases of Mausers, machine guns, revolvers and ammunition ordered in Germany by the Industry Trading Co., 20 Museum Road, arrived in Shanghai on August 3 on the s.s. Hamburg. The arms and ammunition have been placed in the Customs godown in Pootung.

The Union of Restaurant Waiters (Cantonese), whose office is at No. 17 Yu Poh Li, Paoshan Road, Chapei, desires to prevent persons who are not members of the Union from working in restaurants. At 11 a.m. yesterday 50 of these persons proceeded to the Union where they created a disturbance and injured two members of the committee. 20 armed constables of the Fifth District of the Bureau of Public Safety arrived soon after and arrested six of the men.

1929年8月6日。

在关于国家军队遣散与重组的会议上，蒋介石及国民政府其他成员决定遣散十分之七的部队，保留80万人作为政府军。

阎锡山已致电政府，称冯玉祥的士兵不会遵守政府关于遣散和重组的命令。

国民政府已指示平汉铁路停止向冯玉祥汇付每月30万美元的军费。然而，向阎锡山的汇款将不会停止。

阎锡山麾下的第三集团军将在两个月内进行遣散和重组。此事完成后，阎锡山将与冯玉祥一同出国。

财政部长宋子文（Soong Ts Van）与上海各银行达成协议，将在上海发行价值500万美元的债券，以支付军队遣散和重组的费用。本月将把50%的债券投放市场。

昨日下午2时，17个工会的代表在闸北国庆路宝增德里13号中外布匹店职工联合会办事处举行会议，这些工会包括商务印书馆工人工会、排字工人工会、闸北水电公司工人工会等。布匹业工会的郑伯英（Zing Pah Yai，音译）担任主席。

通过的决议之一如下：
“以闸北各工会的名义通知社会局和上海特别区国民党党部，第六区国民党党部正在压迫各工会。”

Enquiries by the Kobe Water Police elicited the fact that two similar tubes were sent to Shanghai prior to this aboard the S.S. "Amagi Maru" on February 25, 1928 and the S.S. "Baikal Maru" on April 22, 1928, therefore the matter was referred to the local Japanese Consulate.

It was ascertained by the Consular Police authorities that Shigeichi Abe, younger brother of Jukichi Abe, Kashin Yoko, No. 121 Boone Road, had received the tubes which were sent on February 25th and April 22nd, 1928 from Kobe. He was taken into custody on April 20th, 1928 and informed the officers that the tubes were handed over to one Kimura, living in an alleyway off Broadway, who was the rightful claimant for the goods. He insisted on denying any knowledge as to the contents of the tubes. Vain enquiries were made by the Consular officials to obtain evidence to charge him with importing arms and ammunition. However he was sentenced to 29 days' imprisonment on April 20th, 1928 for the breach of Consular regulations governing registration. He was ordered on May 22nd, 1928 to be deported from China for three years, and left here for Japan aboard the S.S. "Kamo Maru" on May 28th, 1928.

今年四月下旬，当地日本领事馆警察根据
从神户水上警察收到的情报，逮捕了一名日本人，当局怀疑此人牵涉多起

他和他的团伙采用新颖的方法

OSAKA MAINICHI & THE TOKYO NICHI NICHI, OSAKA, SUNDAY, MARCH 31, 1929

Free Arms Supply
To China Proposed

Japan Opposes Idea; Powers
Want to Dispose of Old
Arms—The Motive

Special to The Osaka Mainichi
PEPING, Mar. 29.—The treaty concluded among the Powers for prohibiting the export of arms to China is likely to be abolished soon. The abolition of the arms treaty was proposed by Sir Miles Lampson, British Minister to China, at a recent conference of the Ministers held in Peping, on the ground that supplying arms to China by the powers would not encourage disturbances, inasmuch as the country has been unified.
The American, French and Italian Ministers favoured the proposal, but Japan objected to it on the ground that complete peace had not yet been restored in China and that the abolition of the arms treaty would encourage civil wars.

Will Eventually Disappear
No agreement, therefore, was reached at the conference, and all the Ministers asked for instructions from their home Government. The Powers, excepting Japan, being strongly in favour of the abrogation of the arms treaty, it is expected that it will be ultimately accomplished. A report says that two or three countries have already commenced to supply arms to China.
It is stated that Britain, America and some other countries have come to favour the abolition of the treaty because of big orders for arms coming from China and also because these countries frequently replace old arms with new equipment.

提议向中国
自由供应武器

日本反对该想法；列强
希望处理旧式
武器——其动机

《大阪每日新闻》特约稿
北平，3月29日。—列强之间禁止向中国出口武器的条约很可能很快被废除。英国驻华公使蓝普森爵士（Sir Miles Lampson）在最近于北平举行的公使会议上提出了废除武器条约的建议，理由是既然中国已经统一，列强向中国供应武器不会助长动荡。
美国、法国和意大利公使赞成该提议，但日本表示反对，理由是中国尚未完全恢复和平，废除武器条约将鼓励内战。

终将消失
因此，会议未达成任何协议，所有公使均请求本国政府指示。鉴于除日本外的列强强烈支持废除武器条约，预计最终将会实现。有报告称，两三个国家已经开始向中国供应武器。
据说，英国、美国和其他一些国家之所以倾向于废除该条约，是因为来自中国的武器订单巨大，同时也因为这些国家经常用新装备替换旧武器。
